I'd suggest searching blog.google directly for the October 15, 2026 post, or trying the title with different wording.

results:
The search turned up the post itself, plus many other Google blog posts that use the same "More ways to connect with the web from Search" banner as a series label.

The main match is an article from about four days ago, where Google describes updating AI Mode and AI Overviews to add clearer inline links and more context about sources. The post's list of highlights says the update makes finding information easier and faster. It also covers a dedicated section that highlights official websites and updated carousels and visual links for news.

Other posts under the same banner cover related topics:
- **Connected apps:** Users can link services such as Instacart, Canva, or YouTube Music to AI Mode in Search, starting in the U.S. (about 95 days ago).
- **Personalization:** Search, Discover, and Google News gained a "Preferred Sources" button for publishers and feed-tailoring controls (about 60 days ago).
- **AI Mode in Chrome:** Clicking a link in AI Mode on Chrome desktop opens the page side by side with the chat (about 186 days ago).

I can't confirm the exact date of the "More ways to connect" post beyond the age metadata the search returned, so check the page directly for its publication date.

results:
I couldn't find the author of the Google blog post. The results don't name one for this post.

The post appears to be **"5 new ways to explore the web with generative AI in Search"** on The Keyword (blog.google). An aggregator page reproduces it and describes the update: new AI Mode and AI Overviews features that use generative AI to help users explore web content more efficiently, supporting multi-turn conversations, deep aggregation, and source tracing. That page also says the features are rolling out now on Android and iOS in the U.S., with plans to expand globally. The aggregator's page does not show a byline, and I'm not confident it's a reliable copy of the original.

A separate Android Authority report describes one of the changes: if the initial summary at the top of Search doesn't answer your question and you don't feel like clicking any links, you can now hop from an AI Overview right into a conversation-style exchange with AI Mode to ask follow-ups.

Robby Stein, Google Search's vice president of product, is quoted in other coverage of AI Mode, but the results don't tie him to this specific post. To confirm the author, check the byline on the original post at blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/explore-web-generative-ai-search/.

content.text:
我没能查到作者。3 次搜索都没找到标题为 “More ways to connect with the web from Search”、日期为 2026 年 10 月 15 日的那篇文章,也没有任何页面给出它的署名。

- 搜索结果里,这个标题看起来更像 Google Search 博客的系列栏目名,有好几篇文章都挂在这个名下,不是某一篇文章的标题。
- 最接近的一篇是 [AI Mode and AI Overviews updates to explore the web](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/updates-ai-mode-overviews-explore-web/)。搜索摘要说它大约发布于 4 天前,时间上与 10 月 15 日吻合,但我没打开原页面,所以无法确认它就是你要找的文章,也看不到署名。
- 搜索结果里出现过 Robby Stein(Google Search 产品副总裁),但没有任何一条把他和这篇文章联系起来。我不能把他当作答案。

要确认作者,最直接的办法是打开上面那篇文章,看页面顶部的署名。你也可以到 [Google Search 官方博客](https://blog.google/products/search/)里按日期找。
